title: Keep a refused alert rule away from the evaluator

blocks.text: At 03:11 an engineer saved an alert rule with a window of `0s`. The API answered `400 Bad Request`, and the engineer fixed the typo. At 03:12 the evaluator's thread died with a `NullPointerException`, and no alert fired for the rest of the night.

Every rule lives in a `RuleBook`, which the evaluator walks once a minute. Make `src/main/java/practice/AlertRule.java` refuse, with `IllegalArgumentException`, any rule the evaluator can't run: a missing or blank metric, a threshold that isn't a finite number, or a missing window or one shorter than a minute. A rule that was refused must never be walked by the evaluator, while every valid rule still is.
About six lines in total: the `check` method, and whatever else in the class it takes.

cases.says: a valid rule keeps its metric, threshold and window and is in the book the evaluator walks
a blank or missing metric, a threshold that isn't finite, and a missing window or one under a minute are refused with IllegalArgumentException
a rule the constructor refused is not in the book, and an evaluator pass over the book still runs

origin.section: A Constructor That Fails Has Already Published this If It Registered Itself First

concepts: A constructor checks every argument before it stores or hands out `this`, so a refused object is never reachable.
